extracted.intended_audience: public relations professionals, corporate communications teams, and clients considering or evaluating PR firms
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and lessons for running public relations campaigns ethically and strategically, drawn from the Bell Pottinger scandal; aimed at helping PR firms and clients avoid harmful tactics and reputational collapse. Focuses on client selection, campaign authenticity, measurement beyond engagement metrics, and consideration of broader societal impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance storytelling with business objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: PR should create or control a story but also keep business moving forward.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public relations helps set the agenda for public discussion and communication with the right audiences; it’s not just about getting media coverage and people’s attention but also about delivering business outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical practice — avoid immoral shortcuts
rubrics_metrics.description: PR professionals must avoid taking shortcuts or using immoral tactics; ethics are central to sustainable PR practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Bell Pottinger case illustrates the ‘thin ice’ pros put themselves on when using unethical approaches. Ethics — not just regret — determine long-term viability and reputation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authenticity in social media campaigns
rubrics_metrics.description: Social campaigns must be authentic and transparent; do not use fake accounts or astroturfing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anti-pattern: creating fake accounts and hashtags (e.g., #RespectGuptas) to manufacture support. Such tactics may achieve short-term objectives but are dishonest and can cause severe fallout.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider broader social and political impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate how campaigns affect political, social and community dynamics beyond immediate client goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bell Pottinger’s campaigns harmed race relations in South Africa and set back public discourse; success measured only by campaign outputs ignored wider societal damage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Client selection and reputational risk
rubrics_metrics.description: Carefully choose who you work for because a firm ‘puts its name behind everything we create’; associations carry reputational consequences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid becoming known as a mercenary firm for hire; once a damaging client connection is exposed, firms may be unable to distance themselves and can suffer rapid client loss.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure success beyond clicks and retweets
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not evaluate campaigns solely by engagement metrics; consider long-term reputation and real-world consequences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Think beyond the press release and beyond the hashtag — clicks and retweets are insufficient measures and can mask negative impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Align strategy, story and messaging with business goals and values
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure that a client’s strategy, story and messaging reflect their business goals and ideals while achieving objectives without harming others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: "Put yourself in the client’s shoes": craft communications that both advance business aims and are consistent with ethical standards and stakeholder interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-way communication and audience responsiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat PR as a dialogue rather than a one-way broadcast; listen and respond to audiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PR is no longer a one-way conversation — people matter and will respond to positive stories and calls to action, so campaigns should engage audiences constructively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accountability of principals and long-term consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Principals and strategists are accountable for campaign outcomes; unethical campaigns can leave a trail of destruction even if individuals attempt to move on.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After firm collapse, leaders may release statements and pursue new ventures, but the damage to communities, clients and the industry persists; accountability should be considered in planning and oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beware short-term business gains that risk catastrophic losses
rubrics_metrics.description: Short-term campaign ‘success’ can precipitate rapid and severe business losses if tactics are unethical or expose clients to scandal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Bell Pottinger suffered £8 million worth of client losses in 48 hours — demonstrating the financial peril of unethical PR choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusive and sensitive storytelling
rubrics_metrics.description: Brands should offer positive stories that are inclusive and sensitive to diverse audiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Campaigns should avoid narratives that polarize or harm particular groups; inclusivity is increasingly expected by stakeholders and the public.
